analysis:
Examined both primary analyses and replayed patches for .github/workflows/ci.yml and docs/developer/build.md, including unchanged file modes. The CI patch replaces one five-job provider lane with five separately requested one-job lanes (head lines 43–47) and selects a lane by matrix shard (head line 142). The documentation patch describes the same mapping and whole-lane allocation behavior (head lines 228–251). These changes allow partial Sandbox allocation rather than requiring capacity for all five shards together.
No independently supported security regression was identified. Sandbox execution and Blacksmith fallback already existed; changing allocation granularity does not itself establish a new untrusted-host boundary, credential exposure, or bypass of build qualification. The supplied changes do not modify provider authorization, attestation, encryption, billing, native inference or cache controls. Relevant model concerns are host/build integrity (TB-003, T-013, T-034, T-054); CI success is not production qualification under TB-011.
Both analyses raise the same unresolved dependency: .github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml, consumed at ci.yml head line 37, must support distinct lanes sharing a profile, emit all requested route keys, preserve label validation and fallback, and allocate capacity without conflicting grants. Its implementation is absent, so this is an unverified integration contract, not evidence of a missing control. Review that contract before concluding the revised allocation preserves runner isolation and availability. Replay omitted four source units; unchanged gates, build actions and callers were not independently re-examined here. Documentation assertions and prior analyses alone do not establish their implementation.
